back_translation: Oh, if only you were like a brother to me, one who nursed at my mother's breasts! When I found you outside I could kiss you, and no one would despise me.
I would lead you and bring you into my mother's house — she who used to teach me. I would give you spiced wine to drink, and my pomegranate juice.
His left arm is under my head, and his right arm embraces me.
O daughters of Jerusalem, I make you swear: do not stir up or awaken love until love itself pleases.
Who is that coming up from the wilderness, leaning on her beloved? Under the apple tree I awakened you; there your mother bore you in labor; there she who gave you birth travailed.
Set me as a seal upon your heart, as a seal upon your arm. For love is strong as death; ardent jealousy is hard as the realm of the dead; its sparks are sparks of fire — the very flame of Yah.
Many waters cannot quench love, nor can rivers sweep it away. Even if a man gave all the wealth of his house in exchange for love, he would be utterly despised.
We have a little sister, and her breasts have not yet grown. What shall we do for our sister on the day someone comes to ask for her hand?
If she is a wall, we will build a silver battlement upon her; but if she is a door, we will enclose her with boards of cedar.
I am a wall, and my breasts are like towers. So in his eyes I have become like one who brings peace.
Solomon had a vineyard at Baal-hamon. He let it out to keepers; each one was to bring a thousand shekels of silver for its fruit.
My vineyard, my very own, is before me. The thousand shekels are yours, O Solomon, and two hundred for those who keep its fruit.
O you who dwell in the gardens, my companions are listening for your voice — let me hear it!
Hasten to me, my beloved, and be like a gazelle or a young stag upon the mountains of spices.
